svg.title: P011 · How much of the catalogue has ever sold?
svg.desc: One coverage summary for the whole catalogue. Three products become four joined rows. Pen repeats for lines 1 and 2. Cup survives once with empty detail columns. Count 4 joined rows, 3 matched lines, 3 distinct catalogue IDs and 2 distinct matched IDs. Cup counts toward the catalogue. The two sold products are Pen and Bag. Divide by all three listed products to get 66.67%. First · FROM Products. The denominator is every listed product. Only the catalogue can supply Cup, which has never sold. Second · LEFT JOIN OrderDetails. Match the catalogue ID to OrderDetails.ProductID to find evidence of a sale. The left join retains Cup with a NULL detail ID and gives Pen one row per matching sale line.
svg.text: How much of the catalogue has ever sold?
One coverage summary for the whole catalogue.
Pen appears on two sale lines. Does that make two sold products?

follow. Double underlines mark the matching keys. SQL excerpts use … for omitted clauses.

g.text: The denominator is every listed product. Only the catalogue can supply Cup, which has never sold.

ID and gives Pen one row per matching sale line.

svg.text: Three products become four joined rows. Pen repeats for lines 1 and 2. Cup survives once with empty detail
Products LEFT JOIN OrderDetails ON Products.ProductID = OrderDetails.ProductID
Which IDs should each count read?

COUNT(*), COUNT(O.ProductID), COUNT(DISTINCT P.ProductID), COUNT(DISTINCT O.ProductID)
The two sold products are Pen and Bag. Divide by all three listed products to get 66.67%.
